```{r}
shoesize <- data.frame(
  Shoe_size = c(6.5, 9.0, 8.5, 8.5, 10.5, 7.0, 9.5, 9.0, 13.0, 7.5, 10.5, 8.5, 12.0, 10.5,
                13.0, 11.5, 8.5, 5.0, 10.0, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 10.5, 8.5, 10.5, 11.0, 9.0, 13.0),
  Height = c(66.0, 68.0, 64.5, 65.0, 70.0, 64.0, 70.0, 71.0, 72.0, 64.0, 74.5, 67.0, 71.0, 71.0,
             77.0, 72.0, 59.0, 62.0, 72.0, 66.0, 64.0, 67.0, 73.0, 69.0, 72.0, 70.0, 69.0, 70.0),
  Gender = c("F","F","F","F","M","F","F","F","M","F","M","F","M","M",
             "M","M","F","F","M","F","F","M","M","F","M","M","M","M")
)
write.csv(shoesize, "shoesize.csv", row.names = FALSE)

##B
shoe <- read.csv("shoesize.csv")
tail(shoe, 5)
##C
str(shoe)
head(shoe)
##D
dim(shoe)
nrow(shoe)
ncol(shoe)
##E
summary(shoe)
##F
males   <- subset(shoe, Gender == "M")
females <- subset(shoe, Gender == "F")
males
females
##G
mean(shoe$Shoe_size)
mean(shoe$Height)
##H
cor(shoe$Shoe_size, shoe$Height)
plot(shoe$Shoe_size, shoe$Height, xlab = "Shoe size", ylab = "Height (in)")
abline(lm(Height ~ Shoe_size, data = shoe))

##Q2:  shoes$Gender <- factor(shoes$Gender, levels = c("F", "M")) evels(shoes$Gender)
##Q3: Knitting always starts in the folder that holds the .Rmd, so a relative path like read.csv ("shoesize csv") finds the file as long as the two sit together. It doesn't depend on what folder your console was in, and it avoids machine-specific paths like C:/Users/you / Anyone you share the folder with can knit it and get the same result.
##Q4: Gender shows as chr (or Factor once converted), which is what I expected, since it is text. ShoeSize and Height should show as num.
##Q5: head() and tail()head() only shows the first rows. It would miss problems at the end of the file: blank rows, footer notes, a "Total" row, truncated data, or a stray text value that turns a numeric column into character. tail() checks the other end
##Q6: cor(shoes$ShoeSize, shoes$Height)   shoes[shoes$ShoeSize >= 11, ]
##Q7: Males have a higher mean height (71.46 vs 65.68 in) and a higher mean shoe size (10.96 vs 7.86) than females.
